The 15 Most Thoughtful Personalized Gifts

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1039 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that it might only be November, but the holidays are just around the corner, and with Hanukkah starting early this year on December 4, I’m already collecting gifts for everyone I love.
  • The easiest way to make a gift special?
  • Sources indicate that think engraved ID bracelets and signet rings for the guys, birthstone bracelets and sparkly initial pendants for the women in your life, and personalized sports merch for the fan whose team is a whole personality trait.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it might only be November, but the holidays are just around the corner, and with Hanukkah starting early this year on December 4, I’m already collecting gifts for everyone I love. Getting ahead of the curve has its perks: fewer frantic shipping fees, for one, and enough time to find something that feels genuinely special.

The easiest way to make a gift special? Get it personalized. Because who wants to tear through wrapping paper only to find the same thing everyone else is getting this season? Go the custom route, and even a classic gift feels like it was made just for them (because, well, it was).

Sources indicate that think engraved ID bracelets and signet rings for the guys, birthstone bracelets and sparkly initial pendants for the women in your life, and personalized sports merch for the fan whose team is a whole personality trait. Add sentimental photo albums full of family memories and a few delightfully quirky surprises they’ll never see coming, and you’ve got a list worth getting a head start on. Here are some of our favorite personalized gift ideas for the holidays this year.

Industry observers note that know someone who takes great pleasure in writing hand-written letters? Make their next correspondence even more exciting with personalized writing paper from Smythson. Customize everything from the size and color of the paper, the text and motif at the top of the paper, and the tissue lining and border on the envelopes.

Engraved jewelry is one of the classiest personalized gifts you can get for someone, especially when it’s simple and refined like this ID chain bracelet from Miansai. I got this bracelet for my boyfriend with his name engraved on it for the holidays last year, and he wears it pretty much every day.

A personalized jersey is a no-brainer for anyone with a favorite sports team. The Fanatics custom shop has merch for NFL, MLB, NBA, WNBA, NHL, MLS, and even college teams, so it really has something for every kind of sports fan. And it’s not just jerseys—there’s also custom drinkware, bags, accessories, and more.

Industry observers note that even if your giftee isn’t super into astrology, they’ll appreciate a candle that’s just for them (or, well, anyone that shares their birthday). If they are into astrology, they’ll love all the fun facts about their birthday on the candle’s label, including their Zodiac sign, element, constellation, tarot card, and more. And all you have to know is their birthday, so it’s a pretty easy gift.

Speaking of birthdays, birthstone jewelry is another classic gift that’s personalized by design. And all you have to know is their birth month to get it right. Brilliant Earth has a great selection of birthstone jewelry, from pendant necklaces and colorful earrings to gemstone tennis bracelets and rings. You can even add multiple birthstones to this eternity lab diamond ring, so you can personalize it with the birthstones of everyone in your family.

In a recent development, for the one who spends their weekends on the golf course: They’ll truly impress their golf buddies with a box of personalized golf balls. And it comes with tees, a divot tool, and poker-chip ball markers so they have everything they need.

If you have the time and want to do something really special, order one of these luxury lighters from S.T. Dupont and get it engraved in person at a local engraving shop or jewelry repair store. The extra effort will show, and your giftee will have something to carry with them wherever they go for years to come.

In a recent development, you’ll have fun playing around with all the features in Ralph Lauren’s online custom hat maker—we certainly have. Choose the color and add a name, logo, or monogram, and the result will be a one-of-a-kind baseball cap your giftee will wear all the time.

In a recent development, don’t just print out a photo and call it a day; get it printed on glass for something truly unique. Upload your photo to Fracture and personalize it even more with colorful borders, templates, frames, and stands.

Ever gone into a comic book store and seen the walls of Funko POP action figures from every franchise you can imagine? Having cute action figures of all your favorite Star Wars characters is great, but imagine how cool it would be to give someone an action figure of themself. With Funko POP, you can do just that—and you’ll have fun building it. You can even get a pair of Funko POP figures, so you can include yourself in it, too.

In a recent development, if you’re looking for a romantic personalized gift for your partner, surprise them with a watercolor painting of the place where you had your first date or the spot where you got engaged. Whether it was a local coffee shop, beloved movie theater, or beautiful outdoor space, it’ll look good painted above your names.

In a world where everything is online and in the cloud, a physical photo album is all the more sentimental and special. Artifact Uprising makes putting together a photo album easy, and the result is high quality and beautiful. It’s something they’ll want to display on their coffee table for everyone to see.

Gifts based on birthdays is a common theme in this gift guide, but what can we say? It’s an easy way to personalize stuff. If they’re a history buff (or just love reading the news), they’ll enjoy flipping through this customized book of newspaper headlines from their birthday through the years.

According to recent reports, you know that person who is absolutely obsessed with their dog or cat? (Okay, it’s me.) They’ll obsess over any gift that has to do with their beloved pet, like this custom sweatshirt embroidered with the face of their dog or cat. Just upload a photo of their pet (you can probably find one on their Facebook or Instagram) and choose a sweater color and size.

Recent findings suggest that A customized L.L. Bean tote bag is something they’ll use all the time. It’s one of our favorite gifts of all time, and it’s an absolute classic.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a year full of niche Christmas aesthetics and newly introduced decorating trends, it’s easy to feel pulled in a dozen directions. But there’s a reason we keep coming back to a traditional holiday style: It lasts because it feels collected, not decorated. Think plaids and woven textures, vintage finds, and gilded accents—a Christmas that feels timeless, yet a little opulent. However, that look can come with a hefty price tag.

Recent findings suggest that I’m all for investing in quality pieces you’ll bring out year after year, and thankfully I discovered that Ballard Designs delivers that designer-inspired feel—without the heirloom price tag. Its collection is full of traditional accents and distinctive pieces that blend contemporary glamour with old-world charm. Plus, during its Black Friday sale, you can save 40 percent on all holiday decor.

Shop Ballard Design’s Holiday Decor.

Industry observers note that whether you’re looking for pretty ornaments and tree trimmings, decor to deck the halls, or outdoor finds that feel polished, Ballard Designs has plenty to explore. Ahead, shop the pieces our editors are eyeing for their own holiday homes.

Your tree may already have all the essentials, but a few special accents can make it feel fresh and personal. These etched glass ornaments featuring a floral design are handmade in Poland, making them an instant heirloom. My editor also loves these gilded floral ornaments that bring an enchanted-garden feel to the tree—perfect for a fancy-grandma Christmas.

Industry observers note that if you already have a favorite tree skirt, the Carol Scalloped Tree Collar adds texture and warmth while concealing your tree’s base. For a little extra height and an Italian countryside feel, try the Toulon Christmas Tree Urn. It’s also a lovely choice for a smaller tree—or for bringing a real tree into your home.

A true holiday home goes beyond the tree. Thoughtful accents can carry the festive spirit throughout your space. I’m drawn to the antique-inspired look of the layered tole tree, but I’ve never seen anything like these garland-clad ornaments with twinkling LEDs inside. They’re an easy way to add that festive finishing touch almost anywhere.

It has been revealed that finding the right velvet bow for a classic Christmas look sounds simple—until every option feels a little off. The signature velvet bow is exactly what I was looking for in my burgundy-clad home, and it comes in three sizes; my colleague is eyeing the velvet bow bell swag for her mantel.

Industry observers note that outdoor Christmas decor can make your home feel festive from the curb, but it’s easy to go overboard and veer into the tacky territory. For a polished look, focus on a few subtle enhancements and accents that work together: This antler wreath hanger brings a touch of cabin-inspired charm, while a faux-wicker LED reindeer is an elegant show-stopper that looks just as lovely by day as it glows at night.

Plus, the seasonal sparkle doesn’t have to stop indoors. The gold foil LED bow adds a little shimmer to a window, porch light, or mailbox. And thanks to this tree cascade light set, your front-yard trees get a magical glow.

Breaking: Buck Mason Just Released a Very Cozy Collab with Sierra Designs

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor.
  • In a recent development, el Niño be damned.
  • Recent findings suggest that you probably know both brands already, but just in case you don’t, here’s a brief primer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor. We may earn a commission from these links. Here’s how we test products and why you should trust us.

In a recent development, el Niño be damned. Winter is just around the corner, and even in a very weird year for weather, I can guarantee you this: There are cold days ahead. It pays to be prepared for them. And you could do a whole lot worse, preparation-wise, than the latest collaboration between Buck Mason and Sierra Designs.

Recent findings suggest that you probably know both brands already, but just in case you don’t, here’s a brief primer. Buck Mason, founded in 2013, makes the kind of cool-but-accessible menswear staples that you can build an entire wardrobe around. Sierra Designs is one of the OG American outdoors brands, founded in 1965 and responsible for iconic designs like the 60/40 mountain parka and all sorts of other equipment and clothing built for exploring nature. Both, handily enough, were born in California—and today they released their first-ever collaboration.

The fresh collection draws heavily from Sierra Designs’ ‘70s heyday, with reworked versions of an archival down jacket and vest serving as the stars of the show. Both are made from lightweight Japanese nylon and utilize a 600-fill-power, 80/20 blend of down and feathers for insulation. They’re complemented by a range of vintage-y tees, thermals, totes, and caps.

It has been revealed that the overall vibe is easygoing and not too techy—exactly the sort of stuff you’ll want to wear in everyday life, not just on some windswept summit. Which is what makes it so damn good. There’s no shortage of high-performance winter gear out there, but much of it falls short on the style front. This is the sort of stuff that’ll do the job but won’t have you looking like you just finished a black-diamond run. Wear it with chinos and hiking boots or jeans and sneakers. To the coffee shop on a blustery morning or the park for a day out with the family. Or, yeah, even in the great outdoors. Just make sure to snag whatever you like soon, as Buck Mason’s collaborations have a nasty habit of selling out.

Sure, it’s boot season, but our jeans aren’t going anywhere, which means these two were always going to end up together. Wide-leg jeans have become everyone’s favorite silhouette thanks to their comfortable, relaxed fit, yet they can easily be styled for a more elevated look. That’s where a polished boot comes in.

And whether you prefer a heel or a flat, the formula works. Wide-leg jeans and boots make a great pair, especially when that boot is an ankle boot. The shorter shaft lets the hem skim the top of your shoe without bunching, so your jeans keep their effortless drape and your boots still get their moment.

A pointed-toe or sleek block-heel bootie will sharpen the look, while a lug or flat sole style keeps things casual. Whatever look you’re going for, finishing your denim outfit with boots is a smart way to add polish, personality, and a little extra confidence to everything you wear this season.

Give your wide-leg jeans an effortless finish with an oversized leather jacket and the perfect everyday ankle boot, featuring a soft square toe and a short block heel.

What Is Smart Aging? Experts Explain the Skin Care Shift Replacing Antiaging

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1558 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor.
  • According to recent reports, beauty terminology has evolved quite rapidly in recent years—particularly around aging.
  • Natalia Guzman, FNP-C, CANS, a board-certified nurse practitioner at Atelier Aesthetix in Beverly Hills, explains that smart aging is a proactive, science-based approach to maintaining healthy, youthful-looking skin while embracing the natural aging process.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

According to recent reports, beauty terminology has evolved quite rapidly in recent years—particularly around aging. What was long labeled antiaging has shifted toward more realistic definitions of what happens to skin and the body as we get older. But the latest buzzword, longevity, as ubiquitous as it’s become, doesn’t exactly fill the gap for those seeking ways to keep skin, hair, and the body looking youthful. Hailey Bieber’s recent use of the term “smart aging” just may be the word substitute the category has been missing.

Natalia Guzman, FNP-C, CANS, a board-certified nurse practitioner at Atelier Aesthetix in Beverly Hills, explains that smart aging is a proactive, science-based approach to maintaining healthy, youthful-looking skin while embracing the natural aging process. “Rather than trying to ‘stop’ aging altogether, which is biologically impossible, smart aging focuses on understanding how our skin changes over time and making informed decisions to preserve a healthy, strong, overall youthful appearance,” Guzman tells ELLE.

It has been revealed that from a dermatologic perspective, Dr. Brianna Olamiju, a board-certified dermatologist with Spring Street Dermatology in NYC, offers this explanation: “Smart aging is about being proactive, making informed skin care choices, and supporting the skin’s natural functions over time. It involves protecting the skin from environmental damage, maintaining a healthy skin barrier, stimulating collagen production when appropriate, and addressing concerns such as fine lines, wrinkles, uneven pigmentation, and loss of elasticity,” states Olamiju. Ultimately, she says, smart aging is about helping your skin look and feel its best at every stage of life while embracing the natural aging process.

It has been revealed that guzman emphasizes that aging beautifully isn’t about looking young. “It’s about looking and feeling like the best version of yourself at every stage of life.”.

In a recent development, as skin evolves, collagen production gradually declines, cellular turnover slows, and environmental factors such as UV exposure, pollution, and lifestyle habits contribute to visible signs of aging. Guzman adds that smart aging means addressing these changes strategically through preventative skin care, healthy lifestyle choices, and, when appropriate, evidence-based aesthetic treatments. “I like to think of smart aging as investing in your skin’s future and being proactive rather than waiting until significant changes occur and attempting to reverse them,” Guzman indicates. “A lot of the time, the latter takes much more work, and sometimes it cannot be completely corrected.”.

According to Guzman, the biggest difference between smart aging and traditional antiaging is the philosophy behind it. “For decades, the beauty industry has promoted the idea that aging is something we need to fight, prevent, or erase,” claims Guzman. The term “antiaging” often focuses on correcting visible signs of aging, such as wrinkles, volume loss, pigmentation, and skin laxity.

Both Guzman and Olamiju agree that smart aging takes a more holistic, comprehensive, and realistic approach. Olamiju notes that anti-aging creates the expectation that we should try to look younger indefinitely. “Smart aging shifts the focus toward skin health, prevention, and maintaining long-term skin quality. Rather than viewing wrinkles, fine lines, and changes in skin textureas something that must be eliminated, smart aging encourages us to support the skin as it naturally evolves. It is less about fighting aging and more about aging well,” she explains. This approach, she adds, also emphasizes consistency, prevention, and individualized treatments rather than chasing every new product or cosmetic trend.

According to recent reports, guzman adds that smart aging, instead of fighting age, means working with the skin’s biology to help it function and look its best for as long as possible. “The main difference is that we’re not simply chasing wrinkles. We're creating a long-term strategy that prioritizes skin quality, natural-looking results, and overall skin health,” Guzman emphasizes. “To me, anti-aging is often about correcting what we see today, while smart aging is about preventing and protecting what we’ll see tomorrow.”.

It has been revealed that olamiju and Guzman are completely aligned on the first step in a smart aging routine: wearing sunscreen daily. “The foundation of smart aging starts with a consistent skincare routine and healthy lifestyle habits. Daily broad-spectrum sunscreen with an SPF of at least 30 is arguably the most important step because ultraviolet exposure is one of the leading contributors to premature skin aging, including wrinkles, loss of elasticity, and uneven pigmentation,” claims Olamiju. Guzman adds that UV exposure contributes significantly to collagen breakdown and changes in skin texture, noting that sunscreen is essential even on cloudy days.

Olamiju also recommends incorporating topical antioxidants, such as vitamin C, to help protect against environmental oxidative stress, along with moisturizers containing ingredients like ceramides and hyaluronic acid to support hydration and the skin barrier. “Retinoids, including retinol and prescription tretinoin, can be beneficial for improving fine lines, skin texture, and collagen production, provided they are appropriate for the individual,” Olamiju describes.

Paula's Choice Resist Youth-Extending Daily Hydrating Fluid SPF 50.

Dermalogica AGE Smart Biolumin-C Serum.

Sunday Riley Ceramor Ceramide Barrier Replenishing Cream.

SkinMedica Retinol Complex 0.5 Serum.

Bio-Therapeutic bt-sculpt Gen2 Microcurrent Facial Sculpting System.

In a recent development, once your at-home routine is in place, Guzman recommends strategically incorporating preventive and corrective aesthetic treatments. “Depending on the patient’s age, anatomy, and concerns, treatments such as neuromodulators, collagen-stimulating injectables, microneedling, and energy-based devices may help maintain or improve certain aspects of skin appearance,” notes Guzman. The key, she adds, is choosing the right treatment for the right patient rather than following every new aesthetic trend. Olamiju includes chemical peels in a very similar list of in-office treatments, depending, of course, on an individual’s concerns, skin type, and goals.

In a recent development, finally, the experts agree: don’t underestimate lifestyle. Adequate sleep, regular exercise, balanced nutrition rich in antioxidants and healthy fats, avoiding smoking, managing chronic stress, and limiting excessive alcohol consumption all contribute to overall health and can influence how our skin looks and functions.

The best time to start is earlier than most people think, Olamiju shares. Ideally in your 20s, when prevention can have a meaningful long-term impact. “This does not mean that someone in their 20s needs an elaborate skincare routine or aggressive cosmetic treatments. Rather, it is an opportunity to establish healthy habits, including daily sunscreen use, gentle cleansing, and consistent moisturizing,” says Olamiju.

Industry observers note that guzman advises starting a smart aging routine before you feel like you need to correct something, but it’s also never too late to begin. “I encourage patients to think of smart aging as something that evolves with them rather than a routine that begins at a specific birthday,” she adds, offering this decade-by-decade breakdown:.

In your 20s. The priority should be prevention. This means establishing healthy skincare habits, wearing sunscreen consistently, maintaining hydration, and introducing targeted active ingredients when appropriate. At this stage, the goal isn’t to aggressively treat aging. It's to protect the skin and build a strong foundation.

In your 30s. You may begin noticing subtle changes in skin texture, fine lines, pigmentation, or elasticity. This is often a good time to reassess your skin care routine and consider professional treatments based on individual needs. It may also be time to consider a little Botox, energy-based treatments, and biostimulators, all depending on the individual’s needs.

In your 40s and 50s. Changes in collagen, facial volume, skin elasticity, and hormonal influences may become more noticeable. A smart aging approach at this stage may include a combination of medical-grade skin care, collagen-supporting treatments, and continued careful selection of aesthetic procedures.

Industry observers note that in your 60s and beyond. The focus remains on maintaining skin health, supporting the skin barrier, addressing concerns such as dryness and uneven pigmentation, and choosing treatments that respect the skin’s changing needs.

Olamiju adds that even patients who begin prioritizing their skin health later in life can benefit significantly from consistent sun protection and an appropriately tailored skin care regimen.

Guzman states this is one of the most vital conversations we should be having in modern aesthetics. Both experts say smart aging is not a one-size-fits-all concept. They explain that different skin types and skin tones can experience visible aging differently, and understanding those differences is essential to creating a safe and effective treatment plan.

Individuals with lighter skin tones may notice fine lines, redness, and visible sun damage earlier, particularly if they have a history of significant UV exposure. Those with darker skin tones may have more visible concerns related to uneven pigmentation, post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, and changesin skin tone. “Melanin provides some natural protection against ultraviolet radiation, but it does not eliminate the risk of sun damage or skin cancer, so daily sunscreen remains essential for all skin tones,” Olamiju warns.

Sources indicate that guzman adds that these pigmentation concerns also become especially important when we introduce aesthetic treatments such as lasers, chemical peels, or microneedling. “Certain procedures and treatment settings carry a greater risk of pigmentation changes in patients with more melanin-rich skin, so proper patient selection, device choice, and clinical expertise are critical,” Guzman notes.

Overall, smart aging should combine science, prevention, consistency, and thoughtful aesthetic care. “Aging is inevitable. How we care for ourselves throughout that process is where we have the opportunity to make a meaningful difference,” Guzman concludes.

The most wonderful time of the year is one filled with traditions and rituals. It’s also a time of whimsy and a whole lot of sparkle. This season, consider enhancing some of your favorite holiday scenes with items that are fun, festive, and decidedly on trend. Whether you’re into retro pieces collected over the years, traditional plaids and patterns, or natural greenery, you’re likely to find a theme that fits with your personal style and how your family celebrates. “Your home shouldn’t suddenly become an entirely different house because it’s Christmas. It should still feel like you,” says Jade Joyner, Founder and Principal designer of Metal + Petal in Georgia.

Industry observers note that with that in mind, Lowe’s carries everything you need to incorporate these trends into your holiday decorating: from classic lights and trees to quirky ornaments and outdoor decor. Below, we’ve defined the holiday decor trends by designers for 2026, and included the Lowe’s items that can help you pull off the look at home.

2026 Holiday Decor Trends at a Glance.

Collected Nostalgia: Embrace kitsch and joy with vintage-inspired blow molds, animatronics, and retro multi-colored lights.

Rich, Moody Colors: Move beyond the all-white Christmas with color-drenched spaces featuring deep burgundy, emerald green, and brown accents.

Joyful Tones: Refresh traditional palettes with unexpected, playful pops of pink, pale blue, and lime green.

Natural Textures: Ground your space with foraged greenery, fresh cedar garlands, dried oranges, and handwoven rattan.

Americana Christmas: Layer plaids, velvet, and antique-inspired brass for a soft, handed-down aesthetic that feels deeply personal.

This year, people are embracing holiday styles that bring them joy, rather than those that just look good on social media—and nostalgic pieces often do just that. From vintage-inspired blow molds that feature beloved ‘80s and ‘90s icons, to trees pre-lit with large, multi-colored lights, this style is all about adding in a bit of your childhood Christmas into your adult home. “This nostalgia trend isn’t precious or perfect. It’s mix-and-match with a lot of kitsch,” explains Janette Ewen, Designer and Creative Director of Parker Barrow Design in Los Angeles, who has styled hotels, inns, and magazine photo shoots for the holiday season. Beyond blow molds and multi-colored lights, animatronic characters from classic stop-motion Christmas films can add a vintage touch to your outdoor decor.

Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer Outdoor Christmas Decoration.

Peanuts 24-in LED Snoopy Christmas Blow Mold.

Holiday Living 7.5-ft Vintage Pine Pre-lit Artificial Christmas Tree.

According to recent reports, just as more people are incorporating color into their interior design, expect to see more colorful holiday decor this year. Think rich palettes of deep red, burgundy, emerald greens, and even dark brown. “Color in general is making a comeback and all-white Christmas seems to be taking a backseat,” explains Sarah Fontanez, Founder of Florida-based interior design firm Pomme House. Color-drenching (decorating in all one color) is expected to be popular, especially among those who like an avant-garde, creative look, says Ewen. If you’re not ready to commit to a single tone, adding just a few velvet-flocked emerald ornaments, deep red satin bows, or even brown or purple stockings can deepen the color wheel.

Adding in unexpected colors, like pinks, blues, or even lime green, to the traditional Christmas palette of red and green can help your decor feel fresh. “Red and pink together absolutely spark joy for me. I love the playfulness of it, especially mixed with traditional greenery, beautiful ribbons, and vintage ornaments,” Joyner explains. Expect to see pale blue added to the mix as well—many designers pair it with deep brown or burgundy. A few ornaments in one of these colors can give your tree a whole new feel. Of course, a few strands of twinkling, multi-colored lights can also bring a playful touch to your decor.

Garvee 12-pack Shatterproof Velvet Christmas Ornaments.

Holiday Living 100-count 24.77-ft Twinkling LED String Lights |.

It has been revealed that bringing a bit of the outdoors in through cedar garlands, rattan baskets, and pine cones is a seasonal look that will look just as fitting in late winter as it did when paired with your red and green holiday decor. “I think inviting the outdoors inside with natural greenery feels grounding and warm,” explains Iowa-based designer Brooke Mennen-Talsma. “Fresh cedar, pine, and foraged branches make a home feel collected and nothing beats the smell of walking in the door.” Weaving foraged items like pine cones, willow branches, or birch pieces into artificial cedar wreaths or garlands will ensure your greenery stays, well, green all season long. A hand-woven rattan tree skirt can complement these elements, while a string of dried oranges can add a hint of color that still feels natural.

Etokfoks 28-in Wicker Christmas Tree Collar Handwoven Rattan.

ZHANYIGY Natural Dried Orange Slices Cinnamon Sticks and Pinecones.

Industry observers note that antique-inspired Christmas decor that looks like it’s been in the family for generations can feel soft and homey at the holidays, especially when paired with traditional elements. “We’re seeing a return to plaids, velvet, vintage-inspired ornaments, paper chains, and classic holiday colors,” Joyner states. Brass bells, taper candles, and oversized bows can also make decor look handed-down and collected, she adds. Of course, starting your own tradition (like handmaking a paper chain or giving your children a newly introduced ornament every year) can make this trend feel more intentional—making it one you’ll look forward to for years to come.

Greendale Home Fashions Plaid Fabric Christmas Pillow.

ZHLKING 4-Pack Tartan Plaid Stockings Holiday Decor.

The Coolest Fashion Hub of the ’00s Was in a SoHo Basement

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that back when Marc Jacobs was dressing the coolest girls of the aughts, retail wunderkind Robert Rich was his secret weapon.
  • It has been revealed that rich's first book, Winona, made with Francesca Sorrenti, debuted in 2023 after he spotted merchandise on IDEA’s Instagram feed emblazoned with the name “Winona.” "I reached out and asked if they wanted to do a Winona Polaroid book, and they immediately replied, 'Yes!'" he recalled over Zoom.
  • 163 Mercer is “directed” by Zoe Cassavetes, the director, screenwriter, and actress, who was the sales director of the nearby Mercer Hotel in the ’90s.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that back when Marc Jacobs was dressing the coolest girls of the aughts, retail wunderkind Robert Rich was his secret weapon. Not unlike Truman Capote and his "swans," Rich welcomed friends such as Kate Moss, Selma Blair, Sofia Coppola, Maya Rudolph, Natasha Lyonne, Parker Posey, and Winona Ryder to his basement office in the brand’s downtown flagship store, documenting fittings and gab sessions with a Polaroid camera. Now, 163 Mercer, a new book from IDEA named for the store’s address, shares stories and photographs of fashion’s golden years just before digital changed everything.

It has been revealed that rich's first book, Winona, made with Francesca Sorrenti, debuted in 2023 after he spotted merchandise on IDEA’s Instagram feed emblazoned with the name “Winona.” "I reached out and asked if they wanted to do a Winona Polaroid book, and they immediately replied, 'Yes!'" he recalled over Zoom. It sold out on day one, and a second printing followed the next year. The experience left him wanting more creative outlets.

163 Mercer is “directed” by Zoe Cassavetes, the director, screenwriter, and actress, who was the sales director of the nearby Mercer Hotel in the ’90s. She met Rich when Jacobs and Marc Jacobs International president Robert Duffy sent her to the store to pick out a thank-you gift for her professional hospitality at the Mercer Hotel, where Jacobs often stayed.

According to recent reports, the duo, who are so close that they still speak on the phone every day, began brainstorming a project. "I had the photos of all the other girls, so I knew I wanted to do a book with those pictures," Rich stated. They considered wallpaper based on the wall collage or a podcast featuring a different one of the girls per episode, but Cassavetes's film background, including her 2007 directorial debut Broken English, made her the perfect book creative partner. IDEA said yes again.

They worked at Cassavetes’s Los Angeles apartment, laying out images on her oversized office table. "It's a lot like writing a script, which is why I say I ‘directed’ the book; putting together the layout was like making a movie," she noted. Rich occasionally asked her to add an edited image, and she agreed. "We have similar tastes, and we were open to each other's opinions. He has a cool eye," she added.

Their bond developed when Cassavetes worked down the street. "My title at the Mercer was director of sales, but I was really a VIP manager. I had a basement office, too," she recalled. Before Latest York's indoor smoking ban in 2003, the two took cigarette breaks indoors. "The logistics helped our friendship, hanging out in each other's offices smoking and having tea.".

It has been revealed that the book features images of regular visitors plus some who came once or twice, and the women graciously cataloged their memories for it. Don't expect captions throughout; it reads in parts like an IYKYK story asking viewers to figure out who is in the photo. "We didn't caption every Polaroid; they weren't like social media posts," Rich explained.

Nostalgia for an era before our feeds made the post-Covid years the perfect time for Rich to revisit his mementos. The book should appeal to members of Gen Z who are wondering what they missed before social media, and those in Gen X who are longing for a time that felt authentic, rather than conceived in a marketing strategy.

It has been revealed that instead of a feed, Rich created an office mood board wall that started with tear sheets and magazine covers of the girls in Marc Jacobs, then added fitting-room Polaroids, which grew more playful, plus newspaper clippings and memorabilia. He likened it to his childhood bedroom, which was covered in Charlie's Angels photos. Cassavetes says the mood board’s special quality was its esoteric nature. "The wall wasn't for a million people to admire. We had privacy. We had fun because we had more freedom.".

Industry observers note that trust bound everyone involved. Rich knew Moss previously, and Cassavetes knew Sofia and Ryder; Rich met the others on the job. Ryder came into the shop independently, and Rich professed his love of Girl, Interrupted. “’That's a girl's movie,’ she remarked, and I said, ‘I'm a girl's movie guy,’” Rich recalled. Ryder's infamous 2001 shoplifting case led to her starring in the brand's spring 2003 campaign, appearing on its "Protect the Skin You're In" T-shirts and wearing Marc Jacobs to court.

Recent findings suggest that "Selma didn't know the others,” Rich said. “We hit it off when she tried on the Courrèges–inspired collection. I took Polaroids, sent some to Marc, and kept others. She kept coming in. I introduced her to Kate, Missy, and Frankie Rayder, all of them.”.

According to recent reports, the mood differed from today's brand-celebrity ecosystem of mutual monetary gain. "It was unpretentious; no one was there to get paid. We were hanging out and having fun. That was the Marc Jacobs spirit: more artsy, less corporate. It was a perfect zeitgeist moment," Cassavetes noted.

Case in point: Rich met Hilary Swank before her Oscar win for Boys Don't Cry. "She would come to the store, and I would dress her up for all the pre-Oscar award shows and events. I put her in a tiered ruffle sundress with a beachy vibe for the Independent Spirit Award in 2000," he recalled.

Impromptu gatherings were plentiful. Once, Moss, Ryder, and Patric Reeves ended up in the office together. "I stocked my fridge with Sofia champagne cans. They were small but potent," Rich stated with a chuckle. An image in the book documents the mini party. Though Polaroids waned in popularity after the brand declared bankruptcy and digital cameras and camera phones arrived, Rich kept a stockpile he used until 2015.

According to recent reports, "Sometimes I wouldn't even recognize Winona because she had a newly introduced role, hair color, or style," he noted. "But I met all the boyfriends, watched them get married, pregnant, have babies, and divorce.".

Getting It girls to wear Marc Jacobs was simple. "Marc's clothes were unbelievable; you didn't have to beg them," stated Rich, adding that the store's cool yet friendly vibe helped. "I was a major fan of Marc's, and that radiated to everyone I hired," including bartenders, who made great sales associates because "they knew how to talk to people." A generous clothing allowance, four outfits a season instead of uniforms, fueled employee enthusiasm.

Cassavetes remembers Rich's relaxed styling approach. "He made sure the girls didn't wear the same thing." Rich credits his former boss. "Marc liked everybody's take on his clothes. Winona would change the buttons or redo straps; he loved it.".

Industry observers note that costume designer June Ambrose's favorite memories include discovering hidden treasures in the basement. "Robert has an incredible eye and instinctively knew what I needed; I could trust him. He understood the woman, the attitude, and the personality behind the clothes," she wrote in an email. "He made me fall in love with Marc Jacobs.".

Rich also gave his editor and stylist friends early access to sample sales.

His Marc Jacobs career began when Joe Zee took him to his first runway show for the brand. "I was blown away and marched backstage and asked Marc for a job," Rich said. In 1999, he became store manager, eventually rising to vice president of public relations for retail stores during his tenure.

Sources indicate that before 163 Mercer became the Marc Jacobs store in 1997, it was once the Tony Shafrazi Gallery, which propelled the careers of Francis Bacon, David LaChapelle, and Keith Haring, for whom Rich once worked. "There was nothing in SoHo; Marc could have picked any space. There was good energy there. Tony would stop in and regret having given the space up," Rich noted, noting Jacobs kicked off SoHo’s current designer shopping enclave.

It has been revealed that "The store was so laid-back and a fun, creative safe space. It was also the center of the downtown fashion world at that time," Cassavetes added.

Rich hints that a third book would move away from SoHo. "We wouldn't just be in the office. Maybe it would be pictures from everywhere.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, imagine a trip to the airport with no lines.
  • According to recent reports, airlines can solve only so many concerns.
  • Industry observers note that the manufacturer has locations in Atlanta, Dallas Fort Worth, Miami, and Los Angeles, and the next order of business is expansion to the airports its clients use most—business hubs, mostly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, imagine a trip to the airport with no lines. No lines to check in, to drop your bag, to be told your first-class ticket is the wrong first-class ticket for the first-class lounge. Now add to that no interpersonal friction. There are no snappy desk workers, no turbo TSA employees, and no graveyard-shift customs agents that give you grief.

According to recent reports, airlines can solve only so many concerns. These are terminal problems. PS, a Los Angeles–based company operating its own luxury private terminals, is solving them. The goal is to get you as close to the charter experience as possible, all while still flying commercial. If you ask around or sit in the common areas and eavesdrop long enough, you’ll likely hear something along the lines of “I usually fly private, but when I don’t, this is what I use.”.

Industry observers note that the manufacturer has locations in Atlanta, Dallas Fort Worth, Miami, and Los Angeles, and the next order of business is expansion to the airports its clients use most—business hubs, mostly. But it started at LAX in 2017, and that’s the perfect airport for something like this. The horseshoe design and the traffic it creates, the small terminals, and the paparazzi culture do not cater to the A-list and executive frequent fliers that use it as a home airport. PS offers a way around that with on-tarmac connection from your flight to its terminal and vice versa. A chauffeur pulls you straight off the jet bridge and into a luxury fleet vehicle; that partnership is currently with BMW. If you don’t have any checked luggage, that 7 Series can (for an additional price) drive you straight to your destination within 35 miles of the airport. So if you are sitting in row 1 of first class, that’s about 50 steps between you and the i7 that takes you to your hotel. Or it can take you back to the PS terminal, which is not a lounge but acts as an über-private lounge experience.

It ain’t cheap: $1,300 per head one-way for the Salon (a shared bar area), $4,950 for a private suite (essentially an airport hotel room with butler and spa service; this price is all-inclusive), and $1,650 for that PS Direct drive-you-straight-home service. There are discounts and perks if you opt for yearly membership, but this is all on top of your ticket, folks.

Sources indicate that and it can lean comically luxurious, with Champagne and caviar offered every time you enter—like before my 8:00 a.m. departure, to which I’m not opposed but which caught me a little off guard. There’s the jet-set marketing—tagline: The “back door” to the airport—and meant-for-the-timeline branded cocktail napkins: “You’ve arrived.”.

Recent findings suggest that but once you accept that PS could not afford to excuse itself from the flex-driven airport exclusivity economy, you can really admire its hospitality-inspired finishes. Its raison d’être is to get you through the airport with as little friction as possible, but it stands out in its commitment to hospitality within those confines.

Industry observers note that for example, interior design and artwork are curated. The centerpiece artworks of each location are done in collaboration with local artists, made to fit the location they are in. The crown jewel thus far is in Miami, where PS took over the old Pan Am headquarters and flight-training academy. The mid-century building is a Miami landmark, with geometric thermal walls acting as the facades and this pinkish sandy and limestone-heavy concrete throughout. Argentinian-born ceramicist Nina Surel matched this with tile-work water features and a ceramic mural at the center of the property. Design like this, small and mostly unnoticed in the grand scheme of things, is what turns your mind back to a golden age of travel. It’s not credit card points and moneymaking schemes—though, actually, you can buy any of the non-centerpiece artworks—just beauty for the sake of beauty.

Recent findings suggest that on top of that, the food and beverage program is considered and regional. The blue-corn cornbread with honey and a ricotta spread that chef Kelsey Kirwin (chefs’ names are on the menus, an indication of the atmosphere) is making at the DFW location overtook my mother’s as my all-time favorite. I would consider the signature PS martini—with (guess what) caviar-stuffed olives—worthy of a place on any hot big-city cocktail menu. And all the coffees, snacks, and water options are head and shoulders above those of both the general-population terminals and the litany of airport lounges within them.

It has been revealed that as far as service, yes, an agent handles your party’s check-in and keeps you abreast of delays so you don’t have to open an app—but that’s to be expected. It’s more in the interim. Servers don’t hover, they listen, and they’re backed by an extensive behind-the-scenes operation: Mention that you prefer coffee, not bubbles, before a morning flight? A note is made on your profile for the next time you visit. Only ever ask for sparkling water when you fly out of LAX? They’ll know that in Atlanta. The entire operation seems to run on Guidara’s Unreasonable Hospitality, the same way all modern restaurants do. If you’re leaving Miami and mention to a business partner that you forgot to try a Cubano (on menu) and a cafecito (off menu), both will likely be delivered to your table, compliments of the house.

But every time I start to get wowed by the service details, I remember the price point and the level of clientele. That should be expected.

Standard terminals are air-side, post-security, where everything (even a fancy and expensive airline lounge) is working within those confines. Since PS operates land-side, with security the last stage of the terminal experience, it has the flexibility to be more hospitable to guests. For example, if you book a private suite, you can fly in, use it for a business meeting, and fly out. Or your parents can accompany the family to departure, hang out in the suite, and squeeze every last second with the grandkids out of your visit. It is an airport experience actually designed around the ways we interact and what matters to us when we travel. That, more than the Champagne and caviar, is the definition of luxury.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that we may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

There's nothing wrong with knowing what you like in bed. Maybe you're all about oral sex, prefer letting your partner take the lead, or simply get more pleasure from receiving than giving. But if your ideal sexual experience involves kicking back and letting someone else do most (or all) of the work, there's a term for that: pillow princess.

According to recent reports, originally rooted in lesbian and queer communities, the term has since made its way into mainstream dating culture, picking up a somewhat unfair reputation along the way. While some people proudly identify as pillow princesses, others use the label as an insult for someone they think isn't pulling their weight in bed. After all, doesn't being a pillow princess just mean you're selfish? Not necessarily.

In a recent development, “Mutual satisfaction doesn’t require identical participation or reciprocation,” notes Courtney Boyer, in-house sex educator at pjur. While some people love being on the receiving end, others genuinely get off on giving pleasure. And just because someone isn't interested in performing certain sexual acts doesn't mean they don't care about their partner's satisfaction.

So, whether you identify as a pillow princess, have been called one, or are just curious about the sex term, here's what to know about the dynamic, how it works, and why there's more to it than simply lying back and enjoying the attention.

A pillow princess is someone who prefers receiving sexual pleasure rather than giving it, whether that's through oral sex, fingering, sex toys, or other forms of stimulation. While some pillow princesses exclusively enjoy receiving, others are open to giving pleasure in certain ways or situations.

The term has been around for decades, with documented use in queer publications dating back to the early 1990s, explains Tara Suwinyattichaiporn, PhD, sexologist and author of How Do You Like It? A Guide for Getting What You Want (in Bed). Although it's still widely associated with queer women, the label has expanded to include people of different genders and sexual orientations.

Industry observers note that despite what the name might suggest, being a pillow princess isn't necessarily the same as dead fishing in bed. “Receiving doesn’t automatically mean being passive. You can be expressive, engaged, and clear about what feels good,” indicates Boyer. That might mean guiding your partner, initiating certain kinds of touch, or being vocal about what turns you on.

Industry observers note that not at all. There's nothing inherently wrong with preferring to receive pleasure, provided everyone involved is happy with the arrangement.

Sources indicate that “Preferring to receive is a preference; disregarding your partner’s experience and needs is selfishness,” says Boyer. Being a pillow princess doesn't give someone a free pass to ignore their partner's desires, but it also doesn't mean they owe anyone a particular sexual act in return.

Recent findings suggest that as Bryony Lees, sex and relationships educator at Little Leaf Agency, explains, a pillow princess dynamic can be perfectly healthy as long as both partners understand and enjoy their respective roles. Problems tend to arise when those expectations haven't been discussed, particularly if one person wants more reciprocity than the other is comfortable giving.

If one person consistently feels like their needs aren't being met, that's worth a conversation, not an assumption that either partner is doing something wrong.

If a pillow princess prefers receiving pleasure, a stone top is essentially the other side of that equation. Also rooted in queer sexual culture, stone tops enjoy giving pleasure but have boundaries around receiving certain kinds of touch.

“A stone top generally enjoys giving with firm boundaries around receiving touch; a service top centers pleasure in pleasing their partner but may also enjoy receiving,” explains Boyer.

So, are pillow princesses and stone tops a perfect match? Potentially. “A stone top can be a great partner for a pillow princess because they mainly love to give and derive a lot of enjoyment from that, with very little desire to receive,” says Dr. Tara. Of course, agreeing on who's giving and who's receiving doesn't necessarily mean you'll enjoy all the same things in bed.

Start by talking about your preferences outside the bedroom, when there's less pressure to make a decision in the moment. And don't assume identifying as a pillow princess tells your partner everything they need to know. Boyer suggests opening the conversation with something like, “I really enjoy receiving, and I don’t enjoy giving certain kinds of touch. What do you enjoy? What makes you feel good?”.

Industry observers note that if one partner wants more reciprocity, Lees recommends looking for other ways to show affection and appreciation, whether that's verbal encouragement during sex, a massage, or other forms of intimacy. Dr. Tara also suggests mixing up your sexual experiences, whether that means dedicating one encounter to receiving or exploring different activities that satisfy both partners.

In a recent development, of course, that only works if everyone genuinely wants to participate. As Boyer points out, nobody should have to cross a sexual boundary just to make things feel fair.

And if your preferences ultimately don't line up? That doesn't necessarily mean either person is wrong. Have an honest conversation about whether there's room for compromise without crossing anyone's boundaries. If there isn't, you may need to reconsider your sexual compatibility. Sometimes, two people can both know exactly what they want in bed and still not be the right match.

When it comes to home design, there’s a lot to cover, from new trends to furniture collaboration drops to specific internet-breaking interiors. One of our favorite things to do around this time is figure out what’s coming next in terms of interiors.

Recent findings suggest that we love predicting what’s going to be hot in home design for the upcoming seasons; however, you can’t talk about what’s going to be “in” without also touching on what’s going to be “out.” We asked a handful of designers to share what design choices and interior trends they saw a lot of in 2026 that they’re more than happy to leave behind in 2027. Keep reading to find out the nine things they noted.

We spend so much time making our interiors warm and reflective of our personalities, it would be a shame to ruin the look of these spaces by opting for one-dimensional lighting.

“It's time to move beyond relying on a single overhead fixture or wall-to-wall recessed lighting to illuminate an entire room,” designer Kristen Mendoza of Four Brothers Design + Build says. “Flat, overly bright lighting can make even the most beautifully designed spaces feel sterile and uninviting.”.

Sources indicate that instead, incorporating layers of lighting to add dimension and create a warm atmosphere is much better for your home. Sconces, picture lights, table lamps, and thoughtfully placed accent lighting at various heights throughout the room, Mendoza adds, give a space a more intimate touch.

“I also recommend using warm 2700K light sources on dimmers to flatter people, highlight architectural details, and bring out the natural beauty of materials,” she explains. “Lighting should be considered early in the design and construction process, not treated as an afterthought.”.

Part of the appeal of “grandma chic” decor is that it’s been collected over time. The pieces show their age, the interior is imperfect, and it’s very clearly reflective of the homeowner’s personality and life. However, “there is a difference between a room that feels ‘collected over time’ and one that feels inherited all at once,” designer Stephanie Kraus explains, and she’s tired of seeing this false presentation on display in people’s homes.

In a recent development, “Heavy Roman shades with lots of fabric, chintz on top of chintz on top of chintz, fringe on every edge, etc.,” she adds. “One of these details in a room can be charming, but if you use them all together, the room can start to feel like a period movie set.”.

It’s often clear when this eccentric aesthetic is manufactured rather than effortless. Instead of trying to make the “ideal” interior in the span of a month, be patient and work on your home over a greater span of time. That way, the end product will look authentic.

Though curved sofas are massively popular right now and look gorgeous in a photograph, Kraus is ready to leave them in 2026. “A curved sofa rarely seats more than two people comfortably,” she notes. “Once guests settle in, everyone ends up sitting awkwardly, and conversation feels harder than it should.”.

She’s all for a sofa or couch being something that invites people in to linger over conversations and stay late into the night, and a kidney-shaped seat isn’t going to do that.

Sources indicate that while designer Maggie Vollrath of Provision Studios loved seeing the return of decorative, playful details like ruffles and scalloped edges, she thinks we’ve gone a bit overboard in 2026. These touches are being applied to just about everything: upholstery, pillows, lampshades, bedding, furniture—the list could go on.

“These details can be incredibly charming, but when they're repeated throughout an entire room, they begin to lose the very character that makes them special,” she says.

Rather than treat every piece of a room with one of these details, Vollrath suggests opting for a scalloped lampshade or a beautifully tailored ruffled pillow instead to still capture that charm without drowning the space in them.

According to recent reports, “Limiting these details to one or two thoughtful applications allows them to feel intentional rather than overly thematic,” she adds. “Sometimes, the most interesting interiors are as much about what you choose to leave out as what you include.”.

Industry observers note that “I'd love to see us move away from selecting materials simply because they imitate the appearance of something more expensive,” Vollrath explains. This goes beyond marble-printed contact paper and burl wood veneer; the designer means on a larger scale, like mass-produced tile that’s made to replicate the imperfections of handmade zellige.

“Part of what makes authentic zellige so beautiful is the craftsmanship and natural variation that comes from its production,” she says. “When those qualities are artificially reproduced, I think we sometimes lose the very thing that made the original material special.”.

She would rather see a greater appreciation for beautiful, honest materials at every price point, and if the exact thing a homeowner wants is out of budget, then her solution would be to pivot the idea altogether rather than find something cheaply made that looks like what they desire.

“A classic Carrara marble paired with beautifully considered cabinetry can create an incredibly sophisticated interior, even when something as dramatic as Calacatta Viola isn't within the budget,” Vollrath explains.

We could probably say this every year, but it bears repeating: Don’t solely follow trends! “Just because something is trending doesn't mean it's right for your home,” designer Drew Michael Scott of Lone Fox indicates. “Polka dots are having a moment right now, but they don't make sense in many homes, or dare I say, most homes.”.

Industry observers note that he suggests thinking of home trends as prompts that should get you to brainstorm new ideas for your space that actually fit your style. Take polka dots again. If you want to introduce a new pattern to your home, but you don’t particularly mesh with polka dots, try a stripe instead.

Recent findings suggest that “If you try to force something you don't love into your home just because it's trending, you're going to drive yourself crazy,” he adds. Let’s leave this line of thinking back in 2026 once and for all.

While we love a good built-in bookshelf and wooden ceiling beam, those types of architectural details don’t always make sense in every single home. In 2026, as personality-filled interiors became more popular for everyone, a lot of homeowners looked into adding this type of millwork to their spaces as a way to add more visual interest and texture.

It has been revealed that “Decorative beams, arches, and elaborate millwork can feel forced when they don't make sense with the architecture of the home,” designer Dani Flax of Pearson Design Group argues. “I think there's a tendency to add these elements to make a space feel more interesting, but the result can actually take away from the architecture itself.”.

A home in a modern farmhouse style, for example, would look a bit odd with an intricate ceiling medallion and excessive picture frame molding. Design your interior around the existing architecture and the style of your home, don’t incorporate these elements simply because they’re everywhere right now.

Sources indicate that the next year is not about playing it safe with your interiors—designers are tired of the stark white home. While ubiquitous gray and white color schemes had their time, they can often make a home feel generic and devoid of character.

“In their place, we're embracing more intentional, tonal palettes and color drenching,” Mendoza says.

You can still have a mostly white house, of course, but take a little risk and mix in some pops of color and pattern here and there, or choose a beautiful neutral wood tone for your cabinetry instead of a bright white paint.

“Taking a considered color, whether it's a deep green, warm clay, or earthy mushroom, and carrying it across walls, trim, and cabinetry creates a cohesive, enveloping effect,” Mendoza adds. “The goal isn't necessarily to introduce more color, but to use it with greater confidence and purpose.”.

Recent findings suggest that this is definitely a hot take, but designer John Maloney McNamara of Coosa Interiors is ready to leave velvet upholstery behind. “I’ve tried, but velvet almost always reads as either a 1990s prom limo or a hotel lobby trying very hard,” he explains. “The sheen indicates every crush and bruise, and it ages into something that looks tired rather than loved.”.

According to recent reports, if you love the look of velvet, he suggests going with a mohair fabric instead, saying it has all of velvet’s depth and none of its shine. It also only gets better with age. And though he knows creamy bouclé has been overdone, Maloney McNamara thinks it deserves a reprise, but only in a rich color that can replace velvet still.

Why Working Out Just Twice a Week Could Save Your Life

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (273 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, you don't need to exercise every day to reap health benefits, according to a study published in JAMA Internal Medicine.
  • The study defined weekend warriors as those who clocked 75 minutes/week of vigorous exercise or 150 minutes/week of moderate exercise in just two sessions.
  • "It is very encouraging news that being physically active on just one or two occasions per week is associated with a lower risk of death, even among people who do some activity but don't quite meet recommended exercise levels," the study's senior author, associate professor Emmanuel Stamatakis from the University of Sydney, told ScienceDaily in 2017.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, you don't need to exercise every day to reap health benefits, according to a study published in JAMA Internal Medicine. Researchers at the University of Sydney found that those who work out just twice a week—they call them weekend warriors—had a lower chance of dying from cancer, cardiovascular disease, or any other cause than those who were sedentary.

The study defined weekend warriors as those who clocked 75 minutes/week of vigorous exercise or 150 minutes/week of moderate exercise in just two sessions. They analyzed surveys of 63,591 respondents and found that active adults—even if infrequently—had a 30 percent lower mortality risk than those who rarely or never exercised. So just two moderate exercise sessions a week can quite literally save your life.

"It is very encouraging news that being physically active on just one or two occasions per week is associated with a lower risk of death, even among people who do some activity but don't quite meet recommended exercise levels," the study's senior author, associate professor Emmanuel Stamatakis from the University of Sydney, told ScienceDaily in 2017. "However, for optimal health benefits from physical activity, it is always advisable to meet and exceed the physical activity recommendations.".

So all you need to do is log 1 hour and 15 minutes of intense exercise, or 2.5 hours of moderate activity, sometime during the workweek or weekend to stay healthy. Running, walking, dancing like a fool—it doesn't matter. While it might not whittle your waist rapidly, science now proves that it's better than doing nothing at all.

Editor’s note: This story was originally published in 2017.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A swipe of lipstick is one of the easiest ways to look instantly put together with minimal effort.
  • In a recent development, as we get older, lips naturally feel drier and lose volume.
  • First, steer clear of ultra-matte formulas, as they tend to dehydrate lips and highlight every fine lip line imaginable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A swipe of lipstick is one of the easiest ways to look instantly put together with minimal effort. Even if you have nothing else on your face, a hint of lip color can lift your complexion. It also works as an accessory or finishing touch for even the simplest outfits.

In a recent development, as we get older, lips naturally feel drier and lose volume. A good balm nourishes and comforts parched lips, but if you want more pigment, many lipsticks are designed for mature skin.

First, steer clear of ultra-matte formulas, as they tend to dehydrate lips and highlight every fine lip line imaginable. They also tend to look flat.

For extra long wear, try a velvety, soft-matte formula instead. It delivers a similar, statement-making finish that's elegant while creating a pillowy, plush effect.

Recent findings suggest that satin formulas perform well, too. The gentle shine creates the illusion of healthier-looking lips, and it feels less drying throughout the day. That remarked, brighter shades like reds and oranges can be a little messy to apply, so apply one layer, blend with a fingertip, and blot with a tissue. Repeat to build intensity. If feathering (when the color "bleeds" into fine lines around your lips) is an glitch, a clear lip liner around the perimeter should create a barrier.

It's always best to get your skincare benefits from your lip balm, but nourishing plant oils and hydrating ingredients such as glycerin and hyaluronic acid in your lipstick will help maintain hydration as the day goes on.

Sources indicate that for makeup artist and Jones Road founder Bobbi Brown, there are no hard-and-fast rules—no matter your age. "It's about your style, what you feel most comfortable in," she tells Bazaar UK.

Sources indicate that if you're keen on neutral tones, remember that neutral doesn't mean beige. "Pay attention to what your natural lip color is. I have a slightly bluish-purple tone to my lips. You might have more of a pink tone. It's really great to find a lipstick that really looks like your lips, and the only way is to test it on your bottom lip," says Brown, who notes that a great neutral should not wash you out.

Sources indicate that revered makeup artist Bobbi Brown is no stranger to creating iconic lipsticks. The Classic Lip has all the hallmarks of a modern formula: creamy, intensely hydrating, and richly pigmented. The 12-color range offers enough variety without overwhelming consumers. Expect skin-enhancing neutrals and bolder tones for any occasion.

According to recent reports, trinny London excels at makeup for mature skin, and this recent launch is certainly no exception. It's a glossy, mega-hydrating formula that reflects light beautifully, making lips look plumper, and it's formulated with peptides to help reduce fine lines over time. There's a full spectrum of nude shades, but we love the bold red Poppy for festive nights.

In a recent development, A richly pigmented, buttery-smooth formula that promises to minimize dryness without sacrificing impact. It contains plenty of nourishing oils to keep moisture lasting without feathering into fine lines. It has a rosy scent, so keep that in mind if you're sensitive to fragrance.

Everything Victoria Beckham does delivers instant polish to the lips without extra effort. This slimline lipstick is no exception. It glides on like a tinted lip balm, adding a touch more color while infusing skin with hydration. VB has perfected the art of neutrals, so expect to find easy-to-wear hues for all skin tones. Glide on, then pat to blend any hard edges. It's one of those formulas you won't need a mirror to apply.

Industry observers note that refillable makeup isn't new, but Lisa Eldridge has painstakingly ensured every part of her Rouge Experience lipstick is recyclable, while it still looks like it belongs on a movie star's dresser. The lipstick formula combines oil, gel, and cream to ensure all-day comfort. The color pigments build easily and sit between a soft matte and a shiny finish. It's unfragranced, too.

In a recent development, creative and image director of Christian Dior Makeup, Peter Philips, reviewed Dior's bestselling lip colors worldwide to create a tightly curated collection of 10 sophisticated, wearable shades for every skin tone. Nude doesn't mean beige, according to Philips, and this line includes a complexion-lifting neutral, whatever that looks like to you. The emollient formula glides on like balmy, satin lipstick but won't budge once it sets. Expect long-wear color without the drying side effects.

It has been revealed that when Hourglass creates matte lipsticks, rest assured they feature elevated colors and sit beautifully on the lips without highlighting fine lines, feathering, or flaking. This elegant formula feels velvety soft, with buildable pigments that stay put.

According to recent reports, sisley's interpretation of a shimmery, luminous lip color is as elevated as you've come to expect from this storied French brand. Phyto Rouge Shine is infused with the finest pearlescent particles in a translucent base, delivering sheer, buildable color and a plumping effect that still looks understated and grown-up.

Hermès Beauty creative director Gregoris Pyrpylis drew inspiration from Hermès scarves when designing this collection. This translates into buildable, luminous color and a smooth, tactile finish that feels like a second skin. Even the deepest shades look refined, with a radiance that brightens the face. Plus, the wide, angled bullet makes application as easy as wearing a lip balm.

According to recent reports, not all liquid lipsticks are created equal. Violette's soft, whipped texture is truly modern, delivering intense colors without a heavy feel. The gel-cream texture blurs out fine lines, too, so lips appear plush and smooth.

In a recent development, fragrance makes a fantastic holiday gift. It’s something they can wear every day, a good bottle lasts for ages, and it feels undeniably luxurious. The only catch? Dropping serious cash on a scent they don’t actually like would, frankly, suck. Luckily, we’re pretty obsessed with fragrance here at Esquire. We’ve smelled, tested, and worn more colognes than we can count—and we know which ones tend to be crowd-pleasers.

Recent findings suggest that it helps to know what your giftee is into. Do they want something light and fresh they can wear year-round? Something dark and smoky for winter? Or are they newly introduced to cologne, meaning a beloved classic is the safest bet? (And we know the fan favorites by heart—as well as all the best new fragrances from the past year.) Whatever their taste (or level of fragrance expertise), we put our heads—and noses—together to find the best colognes to gift everyone on your list.

It’s just sexy. This fragrance is not one to go under the radar and escape people’s attention. From experience, it will draw people in from across the room to ask what you’re wearing. A little clichéd but very much tried and tested. It’s unabashedly smoky and resinous, which makes for a captivating cloud of mystery. —Alfonso Fernández Navas, senior style and market editor.

It’s a classic for a reason. Aromatic and bold. I like to wear it for the important kind of evenings when I need an extra bit of refinement. —Mark Burger, social-media editor.

Industry observers note that fulton & Roark makes so many delicious fragrances, but Ramble is one of my favorites. It’s inspired by the famous Central Park enclave of the same name, so it’s perfect for any NYC native. The notes of forest air, lavender, and lemon rind create a fresh, woody scent that will transport you to the wilderness. It’s sophisticated and lush, and it works for literally everyone. —Bellamy Richardson, associate commerce editor.

A reliable fastball of a men’s going-out scent. Up top, it’s fresh and gets compliments without being an attention-grabbing club citrus fragrance. On the dry down, it’s deep and sophisticated without being too fashion-y and cerebral.

This would be my go-to for most guys. I’ve given bottles to my brother (divorced dad in his 40s) and his oldest son (just turned 21). Gets compliments in both age ranges. —Luke Guillory, commerce editor.

It has been revealed that A versatile scent that wears well practically any time of the year. The citrusy notes are potent but not overwhelming. You need only two sprays maximum for this to hit. —Eric Francisco, entertainment editor.

Sources indicate that snif’s newly introduced Double Take cologne is one of our new favorite scents—and at $74, it’s a much more affordable option than some of the more luxury picks on this list. With juicy apricot and fresh orange blossom at the top, creamy sesame milk at the heart, and a classic woody base, it’s beloved by everyone in our office who’s tried it. —B.R.

Sources indicate that after years of using Ralph Lauren Polo Gold Blend, my wife took me cologne shopping at Le Labo in the West Village, where we spent more than an hour trying out different fragrances. I ended up going with Baie 19, which brings an earthy and refreshing feeling. It paired well with my body smell, which is a huge factor. Le Labo also offers a huge discount with its refill program; you just have to bring your bottle back. —Mike Kim, digital design director.

Recent findings suggest that woody, rosy, fresh—a bright and sophisticated scent I like to wear all day. Plus, if it’s good enough for Tom Holland, it’s good enough for me. —M.B.

Sources indicate that byredo Mojave Ghost smells effortless, and even my friends who don’t usually like scents always compliment it. The bottle design also makes it perfect to put on display—it looks so chic sitting on a desk or counter! —Emma Saxon, fashion assistant.

Ranger Station is a little perfumer out of Nashville, and as such it’s got a lot of country-music references in the lineup. This one, done with the Waylon Jennings estate, embodies the man himself: gruff, masculine, old-fashioned.

It’s a curveball as a gift because it’s heavy on musk, leather, smoke, and spice. It smells like the Stetson Original my grandpa used. (It smells more like it than the modern Stetson Original does, funnily enough.) But that’s why I love the idea. This type of scent has been lost to time, so these days it’s really, really unique. —L.G.

Sources indicate that if you know someone who can’t live without coffee, they’ll probably love a coffee-scented cologne. This one from Maison Margiela’s Replica line is one of our favorites thanks to its nice blend of sweet and spicy notes. It also strikes a perfect balance of light and fresh (from top notes of lemon, lavender, and spearmint) and rich gourmand (from notes of warm coffee, milk mousse, and sweet vanilla), so it’s not too heavy in either direction. —B.R.

Pretty much any Dolce & Gabbana cologne is a winner in our books, but The One for Men collection is a good bet for any guy. The eau de parfum is a woody, ambery fragrance centered around orange, sage, and tobacco, giving it a sophisticated overall vibe that works well at the office or on a date. —B.R.

I gravitate toward gifting warm, cozy scents and this one feels perfectly timed for the season. With notes of almond, rose, and vanilla, this powdery gourmand feels soft and intimate. A touch of honey adds some nostalgic sweetness. —Andrea Ríos, fashion assistant.

Recent findings suggest that this is a fresh favorite of mine I’ve been wearing every day. Iris Germanica and vanilla give it a floral sweetness that takes the edge of the manly musk typical of Legend. Plus, it’s hard to go wrong with anything served in a flask. —Bryn Gelbart, associate commerce editor.

I really campaigned for this scent during our Grooming Awards earlier this year. It’s insanely wearable. Spice, florals, and citrus top and dry down hit in the warmer months. In the colder months, the warm, earthy heart stands out. It’s soft without being too femme, sturdy without the usual smoke and whiskey smells. Lazulio is my latest go-to, a more natural scent that is a perfect blend of fresh and classic in a single bottle.
