It has been revealed that every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor. We may earn a commission from these links. Here’s how we test products and why you should trust us.

Recent findings suggest that welcome to the Esquire Endorsement. Heavily researched. Thoroughly vetted. These picks are the best way to spend your hard-earned cash.

In my life, I lean toward luxury and secondhand clothing wherever possible, desperately trying to get away from all the cheap garbage being sold to me on Instagram ads and the Amazon homepage. I’ve spent years of my life hunting sales and eBay listings for clothes and boots. I’m like an edge-habitat pine growing in the direction of the radiant sun that is well-made clothing, trying to forget the fast fashion slop that lies in the forest behind me.

In a recent development, but I throw that out the window when it comes to sneakers. Designer sneakers are, for me, one of the dumbest things I could ever buy. Even when they are made with real leather, you are paying for a plastic sole that has a lifespan of a few years. I don’t think you should pay more than the $200 price of a pair of New Balance when it comes to sneakers.

Under that price point, I’ve never been able to find a good pair German Army Trainers, which I have always wanted. That changed when I found these. Quince (yeah yeah, I was just complaining about fashion slop, but life is full of contradictions) makes a perfect pair of GATs—and it makes them for $95. I honestly think every man in the world should buy a pair of these.

Industry observers note that this is my real qualm with designer sneakers, and it totally undercuts anything you could tell me about the second-hand sneaker hype market. What you should pay for, when you pay expensive prices for clothing, is craftsmanship. When you buy a Gucci 1953 loafer or Loro Piana cashmere you probably arrived there because of the brand, but you are paying for the craftsmanship. I see no such correlation in designer sneakers, even the ones those brands make.

But a $95 pair of kicks? That’s honest. Even though I’m not bullish on Quince’s fast fashion take on quiet luxury (nor am I bullish on its caviar program), and the fact that Quince chose to closely replicate the Margiela GAT instead of the original German army models, I will let it slide. At $95, there are no claims being made about leather quality, or the footbed, or whatever is going on in the sole you can’t see. They look good and are easy to replace; it’s about as honest of a deal as you can find shopping these days.

In a recent development, the thing about the original BW Sport GATs—which you can get for about this price still, though used workout sneakers aren’t my cup of tea—is that they’re just about bulletproof. Those original mid-century designs made were first issued in the 1970s and stopped being issued around the end of the Cold War, a real feat of durability.

These shoes mimic that Army-issued durability. I’ve worn these sneakers for going on a year now. In that time, I’ve seen many pairs of more expensive kicks start to fall apart, get scuffed beyond recognition, and stink like hell. These have not. The pair I’ve worn all year is the pair pictured in this story. Nothing I say in this endorsement could be more convincing than that.

Recent findings suggest that and really that’s the argument here. When I wrote about the Chuck Taylors I normally wear, it was a use-it-and-lose-it argument—they cost $45, who cares if the soles get holes within 12 months. But here, I fear I’m going to sound like a marketing mouthpiece for Quince. These shoes are $95, but they’ll last just as long as a pair that cost you $950. That’s all you can ask for these days.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Although trends prevail in the interior design world, they also can find their way into other areas beyond decor—such as home organization.
  • As we look to the year ahead, four professional organizers are here to share what they think will be the top organizing trends.
  • While AI has been all over the place, from work to our personal lives—it appears to be tapering off, according to Lenora O’Keith, decluttering and organizing expert and owner of Aronel Home.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Although trends prevail in the interior design world, they also can find their way into other areas beyond decor—such as home organization. Creating orderly spaces can make life a lot easier. While tried-and-true solutions are still around, there are always fresh ways to tackle organizing projects.

As we look to the year ahead, four professional organizers are here to share what they think will be the top organizing trends.

While AI has been all over the place, from work to our personal lives—it appears to be tapering off, according to Lenora O’Keith, decluttering and organizing expert and owner of Aronel Home.

It has been revealed that “AI and smart home solutions were everywhere at the beginning of the year, but there’s definitely been a lot of AI fatigue and a push for ‘dumb tech’ lately,” she shares. “When working with clients, a lot of them are over AI being added into everything. They just want simple solutions that work.” This can include things like setting up a household command center and labeling storage containers.

Moving has traditionally been a stressful experience that you were expected to figure out on your own—but that may be changing. Allison Flinn, owner of Reclaim Professional Organizing, indicates that more people are taking advantage of organizing services when they move.

“You can pack and unpack, but you won't truly have a fully functional and an organized new home if you haven't decluttered prior to moving or aren't intentional during the unpacking process by implementing a system that truly works for your lifestyle,” she indicates.

Instead of doing what a lot of us do—devising storage systems for each individual space—2027 may welcome the idea that you should treat your home as an entire unit to be organized.

According to recent reports, michelle Urban, owner and founder of The Organized House, says that people are increasingly not treating each room as its own one-off organizing project. She says that instead, they’re looking at how belongings move from one space to another and where they need to be throughout the day. For instance, items like backpacks, shoes, and sports gear may land in the entry, get stored in the garage, and need to be back by the door the next morning.

“When those spaces are planned together, the system supports the family’s routine instead of just moving things from one pile to another,” Urban says.

Viewed more holistically, experts are also seeing that organizing isn’t just an occasional task, but something to stay on top of each week. “I think more homeowners will begin to view organization as ongoing home maintenance rather than a one-time project,” says Ashley Bailey, founder and professional organizer at Everything Orderly. “Just like other aspects of maintaining a home, organizing requires occasional attention as our lives and needs change.”.

Flinn notes that more and more people are outsourcing household tasks to a home manager or home concierge. In addition to handling things like doing laundry, returning packages, and making doctor’s appointments, these professionals can also help you organize your home in just a few hours a week.

Eco-friendly everything is still as popular as ever, and it even applies to how we organize our homes. While O’Keith says that sustainability never really goes out of style, homeowners are increasingly turning to eco-friendly organizing products—specifically, by avoiding plastic and embracing natural materials like bamboo, rattan, and sea grass for baskets and bins.

In a recent development, but she says that there is a exception for basements and attics. “I always recommend heavy-duty plastic storage [for these areas],” O’Keith says. “Since those spaces deal with dampness, temperature changes, and pests, other materials could get damaged easily.”.

While it can be lovely to live in a well-designed, beautiful home, if there isn’t function, you might make your daily life more difficult. That’s why people are going beyond Instagram-ready interiors and are wrapping in plenty of function.

Urban believes that progressively more people are bringing functional storage into a room’s design, and it isn’t just an add-on.

Industry observers note that “A credenza can hold games in the living room; a dining room buffet can store wrapping paper and party decor between celebrations,” Urban points out. “As rooms take on more jobs, people want storage that looks like it belongs and does a useful job.”.

As we head into 2027, people are thinking about their budgets more and more, which is why using items you already have as storage solutions is cost-effective.

In a recent development, “I'm seeing more clients interested in making better use of what they already own rather than automatically purchasing new organizing products,” Bailey says. For instance, she recently took on a project that transformed a playroom, but used items the family already had.

“Sometimes the best solution isn't another organizing product. It's rethinking how you're using the space and what you already have,” she says. “I think we'll see more emphasis on thoughtful editing and repurposing before purchasing something latest.”.

According to recent reports, I pride myself on living a busy life, but that means I have to work really hard to reduce cognitive load. I love having a clean home, but between running to events and keeping up with work, it’s hard to remember to. I didn’t think a robot vacuum was the solution until I read my colleague’s review of the Roborock Saros 10R. Seeing the way it took care of her hardwood floors, I was convinced to give the vacuum brand a try. I decided to test Roborock’s newest model of 2026: the Qrevo Edge 3 Pro Robot Vacuum and Mop.

Sources indicate that though the Saros 10R has some powerful suction of its own, I chose the Qrevo Edge 3 Pro for two reasons: its ability to lower into tight spaces, and its more powerful mopping speed. After over two months of testing, I’m thrilled with how much time I’ve saved. This is like having a cleaning service come through before I host; someone’s at home vacuuming while I’m out picking up dinner party ingredients.

Best for: Cluttered family homes or a single person’s apartment.

Not ideal for: A budget-friendly first vacuum purchase or a home with lots of stairs.

Price at review: $849.99, discounted from $1,499.99.

Recent findings suggest that bottom Line: This robot vacuum and mop is absolutely worth the premium for the time and headache saved. It’s great for homes with lots of different floor types, from hardwood and tile to scattered rugs of different piles.

Half of the genius of the Qrevo Edge Pro 3 is in the dock, so it does take up some floor real estate. The vacuum itself is just over 13 inches wide and three inches tall, and the camera mounted on top retracts for low-clearance access under furniture or cabinets. The dock itself measures 17.72 in × 15.83 in x 19.45 in, so be sure you’ll have that amount of space for it to live, plus room for the vacuum to exit and park itself.

The dock holds the mop pads, clean and dirty water tanks, and the dustbin that the robot vacuum empties into. On the underside of the Qrevo Edge Pro 3, there are dual spinning pads for mopping, and they can extend to get to your most annoying edges and corners. There’s also a sweeping tool and tangle-resistant brush to vacuum. A sweeping arm reaches out to stir up any dirt and debris before powerful suction takes care of it.

In a recent development, the camera on top is what makes it a smart vacuum. It scans and learns your home with AI detection that’s pretty spot-on, but you can make adjustments as needed. You can have it clean custom zones or specific rooms, so if there’s just one spill in the kitchen, it won’t head for the bathroom.

According to recent reports, is it too cliché to say it works like a dream? I didn’t know how badly I needed this vacuum until I had it. Its vacuum function is ideal for regular maintenance and surface-level cleans, and so helpful for last-minute tidying before the guests come. And the mopping feature is super smart, especially for homes like mine that vary between rugs, hardwood, and tile. The Qrevo Edge 3 Pro vacuums the carpeted areas first so your rugs don’t get wet. And if it needs to travel over rugs to get to hardwood, it’ll actually lift the mop pads up or physically detach and leave the pads behind.

According to recent reports, when you first set it up, it’ll travel your home, making a digital map of the floor material, surface area, furniture, and any potential obstacles, like a power strip with long wires. You really need to clear the floor beforehand to let it do its best work.

Recent findings suggest that sadly, the map isn’t easy to adjust, so if you’re someone constantly rearranging your furniture, you will also be resetting the map. But if you’re like me and stick to one layout once it’s set, it knows your home like the back of your hand. And then it works swiftly and accurately. Remember to leave closet doors closed or open, depending on what you want it to clean. This makes it easy to adjust if you don’t want it to wander into a closet—it won’t push open a door.

Recent findings suggest that as it travels my apartment floor, it reliably dodges charging cables, shoelaces, socks, and any other trip hazards. If anything, it’s a little too cautious, but once it finishes a pass, you can see in the app what the vacuum considered an obstacle, and correct it if need be.

I love being able to see the exact path it took, so I know if there are any corners it missed. I set a few shortcut cleaning modes with set routines, like Bathroom Deep Clean when I want it to scrub the floors of my walk-in shower with extra strength. The “Happy Working Song” routine triggers a deep clean of the whole place.

According to recent reports, this is a robot vacuum that lives up to its hefty price tag. It’s the kind of automation I used to picture watching The Jetsons. For one thing, it’s voice-activated. I named mine Giselle after the movie Enchanted, but all models activate when you say “Hello, Rocky.” I can give it a command like “clean the bathroom,” and it’ll set off on its way. And once it’s done with its cleaning routine, it takes care of every bit of maintenance. It self-empties into a spacious, sealed dustbin. It drains dirty water, washes the mop pads in boiling water, and dries them with heated air. So there are no soggy bacterial centers for me to deal with. All I have to do is empty the dirty water down the drain.

Industry observers note that there’s a remote control option too. You can either look through the camera of the Qrevo Edge 3 Pro to see where it’s going, or control it like an RC car toy. This is why it’s my best tool for hosting—I can run out and grab the groceries while tracking where it’s headed. And with the included microphone, I can “call” Giselle and my voice will speak through the vacuum cleaner. I could speak to someone while away from home or check on a pet. It’s like a nanny cam on wheels. It also comes with its own light for cleaning dim areas, but I find it does its best work in daylight.

According to recent reports, A robot vacuum is only worth its salt if it’s more helpful than it is tedious to maintain. I’m happy to say that’s the case with Giselle. After mopping, there’s no excessive water left behind. It dries super promptly. And it takes not even 10 seconds to empty the dustbin, mess-free. Washing the mop takes five minutes; however, drying the mop takes two to three hours.

According to recent reports, A few notes on cleaning: you will want to empty the dirty water tank every time you run the mop. Because the tank is out of view, it can get gross in there if you forget to wash it out. I learned that the hard way. That’s the only step the Roborock doesn’t do for you. But light scrubbing with some Dawn is all it needs. You don’t need to change the dust bag often (I haven’t needed to in over a month of testing).

I have to provide a few disclaimers on my use of the Qrevo Edge 3 Pro. I live alone, so I can’t speak to how it interacts with kids or other adults in the home. I tend to just stay on the couch and out of Giselle’s way while the vacuum is running. I have short hair and no pets, so I can’t really speak to tangle resistance, either. I also live in a single-floor home, so it’s important to note that if you have multiple floors, you still have to manually carry the robot up or down the stairs. However, the Qrevo Edge 3 Pro supports Multi-Level Mapping, so it’ll memorize and recognize which floor it’s on and start the cleaning cycle in seconds. No need to recalibrate.

Sources indicate that as far as volume goes: when I’m in the same room, I find it too loud for a phone call without some kind of noise cancellation. But when it’s in a different room, I forget it’s running. The loudest feature is when it’s emptying into the dock, which is a small price to pay for automation.

Sources indicate that roborock’s newest robo-vacuum and mop is definitely one of the more premium options on the market, but it’s worth the investment. The smart obstacle avoidance and self-maintenance features take away the stress of cleaning.

The Roborock Qrevo Edge Pro 3 is such a huge help for anyone who wants a cleaner home but doesn’t have the time to put in the elbow grease to clean every room. I’m so much calmer knowing my home is being cleaned while I work or multitask. It knows my home so well, even with so many different floor materials to navigate. I love this so much that I’d run this while I sleep (if I didn’t think it’d bother my neighbors). And with the current Black Friday deal running on Amazon, it’s nearly half off, so now is the best time to get one!

With those themes in mind, and inspired by some of this year’s most viral celebrity getups and standout street-style looks, I’ve gathered a quick guide to seven exciting sneaker outfits below.

Maybe you’re eager to invest in a new staple pair, or maybe you already have one of these favorites tucked away at the back of your closet. Either way, there’s plenty of fresh inspiration to copy and paste this season. Ahead, discover key pairs to shop (if you don’t already own them) and the chic pieces to wear with them.

Y2K icons like Vans and Converse are quietly making a comeback, stylishly co-signed by stars like Bella Hadid and Margot Robbie. Here, Robbie nails the cold-weather off-duty formula, swapping classic booties for black All Star high-tops to give her cozy gray polo, leather trench, and straight-leg jeans a more casual edge. A zesty red beanie completes the look, breaking up the muted tones.

Park Washed Cashmere Polo Cardigan.

Levi’s 501 ’90s Straight Leg Ankle Jeans.

Zoë Kravitz was recently spotted wearing a black-and-white pair while filming her new rom-com, Die Alive, in New York, styling them with flowy black trousers and a burgundy sweater and scarf.   • Recent findings suggest that an estimated 4.5 million have been sold since the collaboration began in March 2022 (and that figure only takes us to the end of 2024).
  • The latest MoonSwatch—only the third new model this year, compared with 11 in 2023—is the Mission to Earthphase – Silver Snowflake.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MoonSwatch standards, it’s been a quiet year. Swatch has been otherwise occupied with the Audemars Piguet Royal Pop, the May release for which people lined up for six days in New York, police deployed tear gas in France, and which, according to Swatch Group, has generated more than 25 billion views on social media.

Not that interest in the MoonSwatch has gone away.

Recent findings suggest that an estimated 4.5 million have been sold since the collaboration began in March 2022 (and that figure only takes us to the end of 2024). In July this year, some 1.2 million people applied to buy one of the 1,969 examples of its $570 Mission to the Moon 1969, a watch that incorporated 11 grams of 18-carat gold recycled from vintage Omega components.

The latest MoonSwatch—only the third new model this year, compared with 11 in 2023—is the Mission to Earthphase – Silver Snowflake.

An all-black counterpart to last winter’s all-white Cold Moon edition, it takes as its starting point the idea that no two snowflakes are alike.

Recent findings suggest that swatch has developed a digital process capable of generating millions of different snowflake patterns, one of which is laser-engraved onto the moonphase indicator of each watch. So, unusually for a mass-produced quartz watch, every example is unique.

Sources indicate that it also features the complication Swatch introduced in November 2024 and which remains exclusive to the MoonSwatch: an earthphase indicator. Where a conventional moonphase demonstrates the phases of the Moon as viewed from Earth, this does the reverse. The two displays run in opposite directions over the same 29.5-day cycle.

(How useful this is to those of us who live on Earth is debatable, but it’s one of the more original ideas in watchmaking in recent years.).

There are some nice details elsewhere on the 42mm Bioceramic watch, including Snoopy and Woodstock in the snow, a pair of miniature skis at 11 o’clock, and a tiny patch of white on the Earth representing a snow-covered Switzerland, which glows green under UV light.

As with last year’s winter edition, there’s a stipulation.

In a recent development, the watch goes on sale at selected Swatch stores worldwide on Black Friday, November 27. After that, until March 20, 2027, the last day of winter, you’ll only be able to buy one when it’s snowing in Switzerland.

Swatch will be providing weather updates on its website.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the market for Claude and François-Xavier Lalanne’s irreverent creations has been on a high lately. In April, a single wooly sheep sculpture by François-Xavier fetched $2.3 million. Over the summer, a quartet of his frog fountains smashed their $3.5 million estimate to achieve nearly $6.3 million. And the record for most expensive collectible design work belongs to a set of flower-adorned bronze mirrors crafted by Claude: They netted $33.5 million earlier this year, eclipsing François-Xavier’s $31.4 million hippo bar.

Now, ELLE Decor can exclusively share that Sotheby’s will host the first-ever auction dedicated to Les Lalanne, featuring pieces sourced from various collections. On December 8, more than 30 works by the late French artist duo will hit the block in “Les Lalanne: Beyond Imagination.” It is expected to fetch in the region of $25 million.

Sources indicate that “Les Lalanne have become a global phenomenon, changing the way generations of collectors think about design,” states Jodi Pollack, chairman of 20th century design and major collections for the Americas. “A sheep can be a seat, a crocodile can be a console, and both can hold their own alongside the most vital works in a collection.”.

In a recent development, the collection spans everything from a gold-patinated bronze gorilla (estimated at $8–12 million) to a white marble owl (estimated at $4–6 million), and a flock of five sheep, including two lambs ($300,000–500,000 each). Highlights also include lesser-known motifs, such as a playful pair of bronze monkeys with deep-green patination that makes them almost look like jade ($800,000–1.2 million each), and two matching crocodile consoles ($700,000–1 million) that complement the famous chairs Claude created after obtaining a deceased crocodile from the Paris Zoo.

Those hoping to get an in-person glimpse at the creatures can see the menagerie starting December 2 at the Breuer building, Sotheby’s latest Manhattan headquarters. To accompany the show, the auction house enlisted Milan-based artist Gaia Alari to devise custom illustrations for the catalogue, which reads like a fairy tale.

“The story begins in the catalogue and comes to life at the Breuer, where visitors will step into an enchanted winter garden and meet the cast,” claims Pollack. “It’s our way of celebrating these works and the spirit in which they were conceived. We want visitors to look at familiar things as Claude and François-Xavier did and to see the extraordinary in the ordinary.”.

Industry observers note that “Les Lalanne: Beyond Imagination” will be on view at Sotheby’s Newly introduced York from December 2 to 7. The live auction will take place on December 8, 2026, at Sotheby’s New York at 11 a.m..

Inside Anmer Hall, Kate Middleton and Prince William’s Country Retreat

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (896 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elledecor

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There was a major security breach at Prince William and Kate Middleton’s country home on Monday.
  • Industry observers note that local police have already arrested two men “on suspicion of burglary and trespass,” per The Times.
  • Anmer Hall has a history spanning centuries, but the ten-bedroom retreat has been particularly meaningful to the Prince and Princess of Wales during the course of their marriage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was a major security breach at Prince William and Kate Middleton’s country home on Monday. Two masked men reportedly broke into Anmer Hall, their Georgian estate in Norfolk. Located on the grounds of the Sandringham Estate, the landmark house is where the Prince and Princess of Wales like to spend holidays and weekends with their three children, and it was also where Catherine recuperated from surgery and cancer treatments in 2024.

Industry observers note that local police have already arrested two men “on suspicion of burglary and trespass,” per The Times. The estate itself was unoccupied at the time of the break-in, according to police, and the suspects remain in custody.

Anmer Hall has a history spanning centuries, but the ten-bedroom retreat has been particularly meaningful to the Prince and Princess of Wales during the course of their marriage. It’s a royal residence filled with equal parts gravitas and style. Take a closer look inside below.

Anmer Hall is in the quaint village of Anmer in Norfolk, a coastal county in northeastern England about a three-hour drive from London. The ten-bedroom Georgian pile, built in 1802, is part of Sandringham Estate, a sprawling 20,000-acre property dotted with churches, parishes, and country houses, that has been connected to the royals since 1862. The estate’s grand residence, Sandringham House, is the country bolthole of King Charles III and Queen Camilla, where royal Christmases are famously hosted. Anmer Hall is just a five-minute drive away.

While you can book tours of Sandringham House and even rent properties on the greater estate, Anmer Hall is a private family residence. The village of Anmer includes a church and quaint cottages, many of which were built in the early 20th century for Edward VII, according to an architectural guide to Norfolk by Nikolaus Pevsner and Bill Wilson. The U.K.’s Office for National Statistics states that Anmer parish had a population of about 250 in 2017.

Sources indicate that anmer Hall was the seat of the Coldham family until Prince Albert Edward (aka the future Edward VII) purchased it in 1896 to be a part of the Sandringham Estate, Pevsner and Wilson note. The two-story house’s “charming” brick facade, made from red and brown brick, features 13 bays and dormer windows in the attic. The house underwent renovations in the years following Edward VII’s purchase.

Over the next century, the house was leased to numerous members of the British aristocracy, including the Duke and Duchess of Kent from 1972 to 1990, and Hugh van Cutsem, one of King Charles III’s best friends. Following the expiration of van Cutsem’s lease, the property was rented to timber company owner James Everett.

It has been revealed that in 2013, two years after William and Kate’s marriage, it was rumored that the royal couple would be moving in. The pair had been renting a farmhouse in Anglesey, off the northwest coast of Wales, while Prince William worked as a helicopter pilot and while they were expecting their first child, Prince George. “[Anmer Hall] would seem to be an ideal choice in that it’s close to Grandma—but not too close,” former royal correspondent Michael Cole told the BBC. Later that year, it was confirmed that William and Kate would be moving into their new “baby bunker” with Prince George. But they wouldn’t physically move in until two years later, when Kate was expecting their second child, Princess Charlotte, to allow time for a $2 million refurbishment, which included a new roof, additional trees for privacy, and interior improvements.

In 2017, Meghan Markle and Prince Harry stayed with William and Kate at Anmer Hall, “because the sovereign still won’t permit unwed couples to sleep together under her roof Sandringham,” according to the book Notorious Royal Marriages by Leslie Carroll.

Today, the Prince and Princess of Wales spend most of their time at their latest primary royal residence Forest Lodge on the grounds of Windsor Castle—but they use Anmer as a country escape. The family also spent the Covid lockdown at Anmer Hall.

As part of the property’s improvements, the Prince and Princess of Wales tapped architect Charles Morris for the renovation and designer Ben Pentreath—the designer who overhauled Kate and William’s apartment at Kensington Palace, per House & Garden—for the interiors.

Pentreath’s firm describes its approach as one “that draws inspiration in equal measure from the great English practitioners of the 18th and 19th centuries, and from the 1960s and ’70s…but always infused with a fresh, modern sensibility”—and the same style can be seen in snippets of Anmer Hall that eagle-eyed viewers have spotted in the Prince and Princess of Wales’s social media feeds. The home—with its high ceilings and decorative moldings—is painted in soothing, neutral colors (though the dining room is reportedly a deep green hue) and accessorized with houseplants, antiques, and gilt-framed art.

Additional amenities on the property include a pool and a tennis court; Anmer Hall also hosts its own honeybee colony. And one last bonus: The home is even stated to be haunted by its own ghost.

Latest Update: Blade Runner 2099 Ends on a Touching Note About Empathy

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that blade Runner 2099 might not be getting a second season, but the show’s final episode provided a tidy ending for everyone involved.
  • It has been revealed that the journey isn’t without its twists and turns: One person who is the key to obtaining Tyrell’s memory winds up dead, and Olwen’s future hangs in the balance as she gets closer to the end of her lifespan.
  • Here’s what happened in the season finale of Blade Runner 2099.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that blade Runner 2099 might not be getting a second season, but the show’s final episode provided a tidy ending for everyone involved. The final episode sees the show’s main characters, Cora and Olwen (played by Hunter Schafer and Michelle Yeoh, respectively) reaching the Tyrell Launch Complex on a quest to find out where Tyrell’s memory is located.

It has been revealed that the journey isn’t without its twists and turns: One person who is the key to obtaining Tyrell’s memory winds up dead, and Olwen’s future hangs in the balance as she gets closer to the end of her lifespan. Cora’s life as a Replicant also has a few complications of its own, too.

Here’s what happened in the season finale of Blade Runner 2099.

Olwen and Cora spend a large portion of the final episode searching for Tyrell’s memory at the Tyrell Launch Complex, which belongs to replicant creator Eldon Tyrell and serves as documentation about Nexus-1 replicants Julius and Helena.

Inside the complex, Olwen and Cora split up. Olwen finds Clotilde and they talk about how Julius killed her. When Clotilde suffers a fall, Olwen doesn’t allow her to die again; in exchange for saving her, Clotilde shares where Julius is within the complex.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, Julius discovers Cora’s whereabouts in the complex. Shortly after, Julius and Cora fight, and he inflicts a serious stab wound on her. He also destroys Tyrell’s memory and insists that he’s the only one who can extend Olwen’s life, but Olwen finds the pair, jumps in, and kills Julius with a gunshot.

Olwen spends the majority of the series aware that she’s at the end of her lifespan. As a Replicant, she was given a fixed limit to how long she can live and has accepted her fate—but she’s offered a second chance at life by the end of the series.

In a recent development, after saving Clotilde, she later reveals that she saw Tyrell’s memory before he died and knows how to re-create Olwen as a Nexus-1. Clotilde re-creates Olwen in exchange for Olwen having saved Clotilde’s life. By the end of the episode, Olwen emerges from a birthing bag, and she later leaves Earth on a spaceship.

The series ends with Cora and Greta understanding each other. Cora, a human posing as a Replicant, heads back to LAPD and is given a Replicant test by Greta to confirm her identity, but this time, Cora turns the questions on Greta and asks about her life.

According to recent reports, the pair talks about Greta’s doll, leading Cora to come to the realization that the girl is still capable of understanding what it means to love and be loved. Cora becomes emotional at the realization, leading Greta to comment that Cora has high levels of empathy. This means Cora technically fails the Replicant test, but Greta allows her to continue hiding her identity and her work as a Replicant.

Is It Rude to Ask Guests to Bring Food for Thanksgiving Dinner?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (533 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elledecor

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, at its best, Thanksgiving is an opportunity to gather around and share our appreciation for one another through contribution and collaboration.
  • In a recent development, however, there is a right way and a wrong way to broach the matter, and luckily, it’s a topic that the best hosts and advice columnists have adeptly tackled time and time again.
  • It has been revealed that the Post Institute’s advice also highlights something important: The onus is very much on the guest to offer to contribute.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, at its best, Thanksgiving is an opportunity to gather around and share our appreciation for one another through contribution and collaboration. But let’s be honest, any holiday can be a minefield, and there’s always something fresh to navigate—even beyond a dry turkey. One particular concern is preparing a meal that will suit everyone and one large enough to make sure no one leaves hungry. And so, a host may be inclined to ask guests to contribute to the buffet.

In a recent development, however, there is a right way and a wrong way to broach the matter, and luckily, it’s a topic that the best hosts and advice columnists have adeptly tackled time and time again. This begins, perhaps, with the most vaunted of all: Emily Post. Well, her descendants, anyway. The Post Institute suggests that it is acceptable, given the “potluck” nature of the day, to ask guests to contribute, but hosts must “Have a flexible menu strategy...be prepared to be ‘coordination central.’”.

It has been revealed that the Post Institute’s advice also highlights something important: The onus is very much on the guest to offer to contribute. Here’s how they should do it: “Offer to contribute to the meal—but don't dictate the menu. Your best bet is to make your offer open-ended and follow your host's direction.” Plus, it never hurts to take responsibility for your own dietary needs, though good hosts will always do their best to accommodate.

Martha Stewart and Ina Garten share similar protocol. In an interview with the Los Angeles Times, Stewart suggests that during potlucks more broadly, “The host can provide the main course,” and the guests can bring the sides. Using her “duck breast with fig sauce menu” (a multi-course dinner party plan starring the namesake dish) as an example, she says, “One person can bring the braised red cabbage and someone else can prepare the potato pancake or the hazelnut brittle for the ice cream.”.

Garten is enthusiastic about guest contributions, telling Bon Appétit, “I actually love to ask people for help.” She also offers specific marching orders: “I might put somebody in charge of wine if they like wine.” Using a guest’s talents and interests to get to the best outcome is a smart idea, and can even go beyond sweet potatoes and pumpkin pie to napkins or place cards.

Industry observers note that myka Meier, the Beaumont etiquette founder, has an entire treatise on the topic, “A guest who accepts a dinner invitation should not discover the day before that they are responsible for the main course.” Instead, she suggests offering a choice, telling guests: “We are having a potluck supper on Saturday at six. I will make the main dish. Would you enjoy bringing a vegetable side, bread, or dessert?” She also reminds hosts to tell their guests how many are joining.

The most crucial aspect, as with all facets of Thanksgiving, is to have fun and celebrate with loved ones—be lenient, forgiving, and courteous. With a bit of preparation, everything will turn out well.

Dorothy Scarborough (she/her) is the assistant to the Editor in Chief of Town & Country and Elle Decor.

Tech Report: Which Video Game Consoles Are Worth Buying in 2026?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1275 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The video game industry is in a wild place.
  • That’s what I’m here to do, to help you weighs the pros and cons of these (mostly) years old consoles against the current price.
  • The PlayStation 5 is your best entryway into 4K gaming and is the best way to play GTA VI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The video game industry is in a wild place. The biggest games of the generation are coming out, Grand Theft Auto 6 on Xbox and PlayStation, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on Switch 2. At the same time, hardware has never been more expensive. The cheapest latest consoles now start at $500, $600 if you want a PS5 (the most popular place to play GTA), with many going for more than that. To top it off with a cherry, Nintendo just hiked the price of its family friendly Switch 2 up to $500, not 18 months after its initial release. So the question now is: if you’re buying a new console in 2026, which ones are actually worth the cost?

That’s what I’m here to do, to help you weighs the pros and cons of these (mostly) years old consoles against the current price. I personally love my PS5 Pro, but given the current asking price and availability, I would recommend the other, less pricey PS5 models instead to 95 percent of players. If you asked me, two years ago, if you should buy an Xbox Series S or Series S, I’d have a different answer than I do today. And then, there’s handhelds. Do you get a Switch 2 or opt for a beefier PC handheld? I’ll help you figure all that out and more, starting with the PlayStation.

The PlayStation 5 is your best entryway into 4K gaming and is the best way to play GTA VI. Sony has pulled ahead of Microsoft in terms of exclusive titles with games like Astro Bot, God of War: Ragnarok, and Horizon Forbidden West (and you get access to that amazing PS4 library as well). In terms of tech, the DualSense controller is an impressive leap forward when games take advantage of what it can do. The console technically supports outputs of up to 8K resolution and 120 frames per second on compatible titles. For the most part, though, you'll be playing closer to 4K60—or 4K30 in the case of GTA VI.

I've stated it before, and I'll say it again: The PS5 Disc Edition is the best console for most gamers. If you want to play GTA 6 at launch, this is probably what you should get. This edition has a disc drive, so you can pop in physical game discs or watch 4K Blu-rays. Totally worth the $650 asking price, in my opinion.

If all you’re going to ever play is GTA 6 and never buy a game again, well, you can save yourself a little money and opt for the Digital Edition instead. Even the physical version of the game is just a download code in a box. The Digital Edition comes with a reduced price tag and slightly reduced bulk. No extra space for that disc drive makes it the best-looking PS5 to date. Aside from that, it's virtually identical to the regular PS5 Slim in terms of power and performance.

According to recent reports, the PS5 Pro is mid-generation upgrade for the gamers who really care, but with things the way they are now, the enhancements are not worth it. Pre-owned Pro consoles are going from between $1,400 and $1,900 at various major box retailers, and you can’t even find new ones most days.

Certain titles like Final Fantasy VII Rebirth perform noticeably better on the Pro, and most games get some kind of boost, but it’s certainly not worth double or triple the price of what you’d otherwise be paying. The kicker is that GTA VI doesn’t even have a higher framerate mode on the Pro—it still runs at 30fps, just with fewer dips during chaotic moments as compared to the regular PS5. Even if I wanted to tell you to buy one to play the best version of GTA, I couldn’t.

On the Microsoft side, the Xbox Series X is the top of the line. This is where I blew through such technical powerhouses as Alan Wake 2 and Senua's Saga: Hellblade 2—two of the best-looking games I've ever played. The problem in 2026 is that, power-wise, the Series X is much closer to a regular PS5 than a PS5 Pro. And, presently, they start at $800. At that point, I’m sorry, there’s no reason not to go PlayStation.

Recent findings suggest that if you're looking to play GTA 6 on an Xbox this year, I recommend the Xbox Series S instead. It launched simultaneous to the Series X as the budget alternative and, well, it still is... comparatively. The Series S is smaller, less expensive and sacrifices a disc drive. Unlike with Sony's Digital Edition PS5, there are significant tech differences between these two Xbox Series models. Most notably, it's a native 1440p console. It can upscale games to run at 4K on a 4K TV, but it can't run them natively like the Series X can. Compared to other consoles, GTA runs just as smoothly, with just as much detail thanks to Xbox’s upscaling tech, only at 1080p resolution instead of 4K. It’s another good recommendation for the casual gamer who wants to get a no-frills GTA machine as cheap as possible.

According to recent reports, even with a fresh Nintendo console coming this year, we can't ignore gaming's most popular option. Revolutionary at the time, this console combined Nintendo's console ambition with the mass appeal of its handhelds in a machine that did both. The Nintendo Switch is still affordable and family friendly, and it's the only place you can legally play Mario games. Exclusive titles like Donkey Kong: Bonanza and the Ocarina of Time remake bolster the existing library and give a reason to upgrade.

Still, I have a hard time recommending any gamer still happy with their Switch upgrade for the sake of it. The leap just isn’t that monumental. That being stated I won’t hesitate to recommend the Switch 2 for anyone new to the hardware. It’s objectively better and the longevity will be worth the price difference.

In a recent development, GTA 6 might not be coming to PC right away, but that isn't a good reason to neglect my personal handheld of choice. Ever since the introduction of the Steam Deck, the PC-gaming market has been going increasingly mobile. And the upgraded OLED model is still the gold standard—trust me, I’ve tried them all.

According to recent reports, my top recommendation for the average console gamer is the Steam Deck OLED. It runs on Valve's SteamOS, so you don't even have to worry about learning Windows (like some kind of PC gamer). The Steam Deck UI completely console-ifies your entire Steam library and makes it easy for newbies to jump in. If you're used to the Switch, you may find it to be a bit beefy, but once I got used to it, I actually found the Steam Deck OLED to be the most ergonomic of all PC-gaming handhelds.

Recent findings suggest that it's never been a better time to get your feet wet, buy some games on Steam (wait for a sale; there will be plenty), and see what all the fuss is about. If the price looks prohibitive and you don't care much about graphics, get the cheaper LCD model while it's still being sold.

Here at Esquire, we compile our guides by performing heavy research and testing, and the gadgets we choose to award are what we’d spend our own money on. We choose the best tech for you based on our experience. We know which little details are deal-breakers and can help you separate the nice-to-haves from the needs.

In a recent development, sauron is blazing a path of destruction in The Rings of Power season 3, which sees him continuing to wage war against the Elves—and the stakes are even higher as he gets closer and closer to forging the One Ring to rule them all. But does that mean the show will return for a fourth season?

Here’s everything we know so far about The Rings of Power season 4.

Yes! On November 24, Prime Video confirmed that The Rings of Power will return for season 4. According to The Wrap, “Pre-production is underway on the fourth installment, with filming slated to begin this spring Shepperton Studios in the U.K.”.

There are no details about what will happen in the next season of The Rings of Power, but the finale hints that the mounting war between Sauron and the Elves could continue into season 4.

In the final moments of the finale, Sauron enters a battle with Pharazôn without his ring on. Gil-Galad remarks that he’s in the presence of the “doom of men” the moment that Sauron surrenders with his head bowed before Pharazôn. The king and his soldiers laugh, but Sauron smiles to himself, hinting that he might be one step ahead.

Industry observers note that until more details emerge, the season 3 logline reads, “All the peoples of Middle-Earth are engaged in the heroic struggle against Sauron and his army of Orcs. His terrifying Ring-servants, the Nazgnagôl, roam Middle-Earth clad in black armor as tensions rise among the Elves trying desperately to hold the front lines; familial ties are strained among the Dwarves in Khazad-dûm; political factions push the island kingdom of Númenor to the brink of civil war; and in the eastern lands of Rhûn, Gandalf enlists his full powers of magic and persuasion as he fights to turn the tide of impending darkness.”.

No returning cast members have been confirmed for The Rings of Power season 4 yet, but fans will be expecting Morfydd Clark, Charlie Vickers, Robert Aramayo, Owain Arthur, Sophia Nomvete, Lloyd Owen, Benjamin Walker, Markella Kavenagh, Maxim Baldry, Daniel Weyman, Andrew Richardson, Zubin Varla, Adam Young, Simon Pegg, and Jamie Campbell Bower to return to their roles.
